title: Codect diff document v2
description: Changed canonical projections between commit, index, worktree, and empty snapshots, including file moves. Consumers must reject an unknown schema version and may accept additive fields. Same-path files with equal projections are omitted. A move is emitted when at least one requested-mode projection is nonempty, with `equal` saying whether its two canonical projections match; a move with two empty requested-mode projections is omitted. Path strings use Codect's injective display form: a literal backslash is doubled, newline/CR/tab use `\n`/`\r`/`\t`, other ASCII controls including DEL use uppercase `\xNN`, invalid UTF-8 bytes use uppercase `\xNN`, and ordinary Unicode is unchanged; JSON then applies its own string escaping. Path bytes, ordering, and identity remain the raw repository bytes. Lines are one-based and byte offsets zero-based. Mutable snapshot IDs name the input kind, not a durable content hash; consumers must refresh them after writes or staging.

mode.description: The projection mode requested on the command line. `tests` is the Signatures projection restricted to test declarations, and is recognized for Rust and Python only; other languages retain nothing, so they project to an empty declaration list. Note that `tests` widens this enum's value set within `codect.diff.v2` rather than adding a field: a consumer that validates `mode` against the enum will reject `tests` as an unknown value, which is the intended loud failure.

merge_base.description: Present and true only on the base snapshot of a `--merge-base` diff. It marks that `id` is the merge base of the requested `revision` and the target revision, not the tip of `revision`. Additive; omitted when the base is compared exactly as requested.

path.description: The target-side display and selection key in Codect's injective escaped form: literal backslashes are doubled, ASCII controls use mnemonics or uppercase \xNN, invalid UTF-8 bytes use uppercase \xNN, and ordinary Unicode is unchanged; JSON applies its own string escaping on top. For a deletion, the removed path. For a move, the destination path; `old_path` carries the source path.

old_path.description: The source path of a move, using the same injective escaped display form as `path`. Present only when `status` is `moved`; absent for every other status. JSON Schema cannot compare two property values, so producers and tests must additionally ensure `old_path` is distinct from `path` in both raw bytes and escaped form.

equal.description: For a move, whether the two canonical projection texts are byte-for-byte equal. Always false for added, deleted, and modified files.

text.description: The exact canonical text this file emits in text mode for the requested mode.

items.description: The requested-mode projected items, including index-only nested entries.

stable_key.description: The declaration's identity within its file. Unique within this file, but not necessarily across the repository (Rust impl keys are not path-namespaced), so consumers key global state by (path, stable_key).

parent_key.description: The stable_key of the containing declaration, or null at top level.

canonical_text.description: The item's canonical fragment. A nested item's fragment carries its container indentation.

stable_key.description: The declaration's identity within its file. Unique within this file, but not necessarily across the repository (Rust impl keys are not path-namespaced), so consumers key global state by (path, stable_key).

parent_key.description: The stable_key of the containing declaration, or null at top level.

signature.description: The declaration's canonical fragment from the Signatures superset projection. A nested declaration's fragment carries its container indentation. Single line where the canonical form is single line. This is the closed-fold text only when `retained_in_mode` is false; when it is true, the mode-correct closed-fold text is the matching `projection.items[].canonical_text`, which differs for container declarations (trait/impl/module) because the requested mode may omit members the superset shows.

retained_in_mode.description: True when the requested mode's projection retains this stable_key.

start_line.description: One-based first line of the declaration node. Preceding attributes, decorators, `{-# ... #-}` pragmas, and doc comments are excluded even though `signature` may include them; an editor should extend a fold start upward over those lines. A `decorator_start_line` field may be added additively within `codect.show.v1` later.

end_line.description: One-based last line of the declaration, including its body. For a brace language this is the closing brace; for Python it is the last line of the suite.

start_byte.description: Zero-based first byte of the declaration in the decoded UTF-8 source.

end_byte.description: Zero-based end byte (exclusive) of the declaration in the decoded UTF-8 source.

kind.description: The exhaustive declaration kind. Every ItemKind in base maps to exactly one value.
